public-growth.name: Economic growth
public-growth.description: Compare ten years of World Bank growth data for three countries, moving from trends to grouped columns and bars while retaining negative growth.
public-growth.dataNote: Annual real GDP growth for China, Germany and the US, 2014–2023: 30 records. Values are already percentages. Country growth rates cannot be added or stacked. Source: World Bank WDI, CC BY 4.0; downloaded 2026-09-11.

public-penguins.name: Penguin body mass
public-penguins.description: Explore raw measurements from three penguin species through observations, quartiles and density, preserving sample identities throughout.
public-penguins.dataNote: The Palmer Penguins source has 344 rows: 342 measured body masses and two missing values at source rows 5 and 273. Missing values are not zeros. Other columns and source row numbers are retained. Download the 342 observations or the full 344-row source. Gorman et al. (2014), curated by Horst et al., CC0.

method-agreement.name: Method agreement
method-agreement.description: Move paired measurements from a scatter plot to means and differences, then inspect ranked differences and individual pairs.
method-agreement.dataNote: Enter a unique sample ID and two measurements in the same unit. Differences always use A−B. Agreement limits are not confidence intervals.

measurement-review.name: Measurement review
measurement-review.description: Inspect each measurement pair, locate large differences and return to the overall measurement range.
measurement-review.dataNote: Enter readings from two named instruments for the same object. Retain raw values; do not pair unrelated objects by row position.

prediction-diagnostics.name: Prediction diagnostics
prediction-diagnostics.description: Move observed and predicted values to residual coordinates, then compare absolute errors and ranked samples.
prediction-diagnostics.dataNote: Enter completed predictions. Residuals are observed minus predicted; sample IDs remain stable and the model is not refitted.

forecast-review.name: Forecast review
forecast-review.description: Locate dates with large errors, then examine overprediction and underprediction against the predicted values.
forecast-review.dataNote: Enter date IDs, actual demand and the original advance forecasts in the same unit. Do not replace them with later revisions.

classification-diagnostics.name: Classification diagnostics
classification-diagnostics.description: Expand the count matrix into bubbles, then regroup by actual and predicted classes to compare errors under different denominators.
classification-diagnostics.relation: Same count matrix · Actual and predicted
classification-diagnostics.dataNote: Enter a complete actual×predicted count square, including measured zeros. Every regrouping identifies its denominator; classes without predicted samples remain undefined.

recognition-review.name: Recognition review
recognition-review.description: Inspect the origins of predicted classes, then return to the full matrix to verify counts and error destinations.
recognition-review.dataNote: Use for recognition reviews and annotation checks. Class names must match across rows and columns; counts are not probability scores.

duration-distribution.name: Duration distribution
duration-distribution.description: Move raw durations from an equal-width histogram to frequency, cumulative bars and the exact empirical distribution.
duration-distribution.relation: Same observations · Bins and cumulative shares
duration-distribution.dataNote: Enter a unique ID and one measured duration per row, not preaggregated frequencies. Bin boundaries are shared; ECDF retains actual observations and ties.

assay-distribution.name: Assay distribution
assay-distribution.description: Compare cumulative proportions with frequencies to inspect concentration and tails, then check cumulative shares at bin upper bounds.
assay-distribution.relation: Same experimental samples · Exact and binned distributions
assay-distribution.dataNote: Enter original measurements and their unit. ECDF is neither smoothed nor binned; the histogram retains all samples and the common range.

classifier-comparison.name: Model discrimination
classifier-comparison.description: Compare ROC and PR on the same test set, then inspect score thresholds and the trade-off between detection and false alarms.
classifier-comparison.dataNote: Enter model, sample ID, actual label and score. Models must use the same samples. Higher scores indicate the positive class; tied scores are processed together.

probability-reliability.name: Probability reliability
probability-reliability.description: Inspect discrimination before checking reliability in probability bins. Threshold points contract before bins unfold.
probability-reliability.dataNote: Use held-out 0/1 labels and predicted probabilities in [0,1]. ROC, PR and calibration answer different questions. Empty bins remain gaps and bin sample sizes stay visible.

correlation-exploration.name: Correlation exploration
correlation-exploration.description: Remove symmetric duplicates from the heatmap, read strength through circle areas and rank unique variable pairs.
correlation-exploration.relation: Same complete samples · Stable variable pairs
correlation-exploration.dataNote: Enter sample IDs, variable names and raw values, with all variables for every sample. Pearson r is calculated; constant variables remain undefined rather than zero.

metric-redundancy.name: Related metrics
metric-redundancy.description: Find strong linear associations in the pair ranking, then inspect the bubble matrix and full heatmap.
metric-redundancy.relation: Same objects · Pairwise and overall structure
metric-redundancy.dataNote: Use the same observation window for each object's metrics and include units in variable names. Ranking uses |r|. Correlation is not a causal conclusion or an automatic reason to delete a metric.

scale-relationship.name: Position and scale
scale-relationship.description: Compare two measurements, then expand each observation using its real size while preserving its position and identity.
scale-relationship.dataNote: One object per row: name, group, X, Y and a real size measurement. Bubble area represents size. Give each axis its measurement and unit.

calibration-study.name: Linear calibration
calibration-study.description: Move from raw observations to a linear fit and a mean-response confidence band. Observed points stay at their measured positions.
calibration-study.dataNote: Enter a unique name, X and Y for each independent observation. Uses one-variable OLS and a Student t mean-response interval. Check linearity and independence assumptions first.

sample-distributions.name: Reading distributions
sample-distributions.description: Move raw samples through swarm, box, violin and raincloud plots to compare detail with statistical summaries.
sample-distributions.relation: Same raw samples · Distribution and summary
sample-distributions.dataNote: Enter one group and raw observation per row. Quartiles, 1.5 × IQR whiskers and shared-bandwidth density use these same samples; duplicates and outliers are retained.

replicate-summary.name: Replicates and spread
replicate-summary.description: Start with independent experimental observations, reveal mean and SD, then compare the median and quartiles.
replicate-summary.relation: Same independent replicates · SD and quartiles
replicate-summary.dataNote: Enter unique sample names, groups and measured values. Sample SD uses n−1. Density is unavailable when sample size is insufficient; SD is not a confidence interval.

estimate-comparison.name: Estimates and uncertainty
estimate-comparison.description: Read estimates, expand their supplied bounds, then rotate the interval comparison to a vertical axis.
estimate-comparison.dataNote: Enter label, estimate, low and high. State what the interval means. Bounds must come from your analysis; missing bounds are not estimated automatically.

ratio-effects.name: Ratio effects
ratio-effects.description: Move ratio estimates between points, forest-style intervals and vertical intervals while retaining a logarithmic scale.
ratio-effects.dataNote: Enter study names, ratio effects, calculated bounds and sample sizes. All bounds and effects must be positive; reference is 1. Sample size is not a weight and effects are not pooled.

paired-evaluation.name: Before and after
paired-evaluation.description: Follow paired observations from connected endpoints to paired bars and each object's change.
paired-evaluation.dataNote: Three columns: object, before and after. Use unique names, matching units and complete pairs. Any of the five encodings may be selected directly.

paired-study.name: Paired samples
paired-study.description: Retain both measurements for each sample, then align the first to zero to inspect individual changes.
paired-study.dataNote: Enter a unique sample, first measurement and second measurement. Supports up to 50 pairs. Do not pair unrelated groups by row order. No significance test is generated.

research-budget.name: Research budget
research-budget.description: Unfold a two-level budget from radial sectors to an icicle and then compare child amounts by area.
research-budget.dataNote: Three columns: parent, child and amount. Enter children only; parent totals are calculated. Each expense belongs to one child and uses the same unit.

unit-counts.name: Counting units
unit-counts.description: Split each bar into countable dots, then combine them again. One dot represents one exact unit.
unit-counts.relation: Same data · One dot per unit
unit-counts.dataNote: Two columns: category and count. Use integers from 0 to 50, up to 12 categories. Dots sort by count while retaining category colors.

inventory.name: Inventory changes
inventory.description: After a stock change, retain the new level until the next event. Step width follows actual elapsed time.
inventory.relation: Same data · State persists after each change
inventory.dataNote: Two columns: change date and resulting inventory. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD. Enter the resulting stock level, not the increment. Keep unobserved values blank.

cyclic.name: Cyclic patterns
cyclic.description: Wrap visits measured every two hours around a complete daily cycle.
cyclic.relation: Same data · Equally spaced full cycle
cyclic.dataNote: Two columns: cycle position and nonnegative value, in cycle order. Only repeating data suits a closed loop. Radius encodes value.

channel-comparison.name: Channel comparisons
channel-comparison.description: Move from components within channels to channel totals and shares. Horizontal layouts leave more room for names.
channel-comparison.dataNote: Three columns: channel, revenue component and amount. Include every component for each channel. Amounts must share a unit and not overlap. Shares are calculated from raw amounts.

series-revenue.name: Revenue by channel
series-revenue.description: Compare quarterly series, overall scale and changing shares, maintaining each component's identity.
series-revenue.dataNote: Three columns: period, series and value. Include every channel in each period, in matching units without overlap. Percentages derive from amounts; raw values remain in the table.

series-change.name: Multiple trends
series-change.description: Compare monthly changes in two business lines, retaining negative values, zeros and missing months.
series-change.relation: Same data · Signed and missing values
series-change.dataNote: Three columns: month, business line and net change. Include both lines in each period. Leave unobserved values blank; negative means decrease, while zero means measured no change.

monthly.name: Monthly trends
monthly.description: Follow one metric across a year, from monthly quantities to trends. Missing months retain gaps.
monthly.dataNote: Two columns: month and value, in time order. Leave unobserved months blank rather than entering 0.

channels.name: Channel mix
channels.description: Compare nonoverlapping channel revenues for one period, then inspect their shares of the whole.
channels.dataNote: Two columns: channel and revenue. Use consistent definitions and additive amounts. Do not include an extra total row.

comparison.name: Period comparison
comparison.description: Compare the same channels across two quarters using fixed scales and stable category colors.
comparison.dataNote: Enter each quarter's data in its own step. Keep channel correspondence; new and removed channels enter or exit independently.

contribution.name: Cumulative contribution
contribution.description: Move from individual expenses to cumulative shares and their contribution to the total.
contribution.dataNote: Two columns: expense item and amount. Use nonoverlapping positive expenses without a precomputed total row.

cashflow.name: Cash flow
cashflow.description: Inspect monthly net cash flow around a common zero baseline, retaining positive values, negatives and zeros.
cashflow.dataNote: Two columns: month and net cash flow (inflows minus outflows). Retain negative signs; use 0 only for a measured zero.

conversion.name: Conversion stages
conversion.description: Track the same visitor cohort from visits to payment in stage order.
conversion.dataNote: Two columns: stage and count. Each stage must come from the preceding stage's cohort. Do not combine unrelated populations.

essential.name: Bars, lines and shares
essential.description: Observe contours transforming between columns, lines and sectors.

classic.name: Classic morphs
classic.description: Eight original encodings with their established morph behavior.

flow.name: Lines and areas
flow.description: Collapse columns into a line, unfold the area and regroup.

radial.name: Radial forms
radial.description: Explore geometric changes between circles, sectors and rectangles.

compare.name: Quantity and contribution
compare.description: Track categories from individual comparisons to cumulative contribution.

geometry.name: Shares and geometry
geometry.description: Unfold sectors into a grid, then gather them into radial contours.

serial-diagnostics.name: ACF and PACF diagnostics
serial-diagnostics.description: Retract to zero, change estimator and return on the same coefficient axis.
serial-diagnostics.dataNote: Complete equally spaced period/value sequence in acquisition order. Fixed [-1,1] coefficient axis and unchanged maximum lag.

interval-story.name: Estimates and uncertainty
interval-story.description: Expand supplied intervals from point estimates, rotate and return.
interval-story.dataNote: Supply estimates, lower and upper bounds with an explicit interval definition.

distribution-story.name: Reading distributions
distribution-story.description: Expand quartiles and density around the same original samples, then return.
distribution-story.dataNote: Each row is an original sample. Retain sample IDs through all summaries.

matrix-story.name: Reading the indicator matrix
matrix-story.description: Compare cell color and area while retaining the original values.
matrix-story.dataNote: One nonnegative original value per row/column combination; missing values remain missing.
